source.note: First training calibration checkpoint reconstructed from the user's 2026-09-01 movement session. Exact clock times were not supplied, so only within-session order is preserved.

session_summary: Restarted physical training as a calibration session focused on hip mobility, pelvic positioning, core control, and rebuilding body awareness rather than workout volume.
context: Long-term sitting and a tendency for quads/calves to dominate exercise were part of the training context.
The intended progression order was hip release -> core stability -> glute activation -> whole-body strength -> run/walk cardio -> foot-arch stability.
The session prioritized low-load, low-risk movement learning over intensity.

observations.observed: With a yoga block under the right knee, the user reported a very clear stretch in the upper thigh/groin area on the kneeling side.
observations.response: Padding improved comfort/stability and made the target stretch easier to perceive.
observations.user_wording: 上大腿/腹股沟位置的拉伸感很清楚

observations.observed: The user learned the small pelvis-as-a-bowl motion: anterior tilt increases lumbar arch; posterior tilt gently brings the pelvis under without permanently holding that position.
observations.response: Pelvic positioning became a distinct movement concept rather than an abstract cue.

observations.observed: During early dead-bug attempts, arm joints popped and the user could barely feel the core; the movement initially felt like arms and legs moving rather than trunk stabilization.
observations.response: The drill was regressed to brace breathing, hand-vs-thigh isometrics, and small-range heel taps.
observations.user_wording: 核心几乎感觉不到，像只是胳膊腿在动

observations.observed: The low back could remain stable during the heel-tap regression, but the shoulders and upper trapezius became noticeably active and fatigued.
observations.response: Hands were moved to the lower ribs/abdomen, shoulder pressure into the floor was removed, and leg-lowering range was reduced.
observations.user_wording: 腰能稳住，但是肩膀/上斜方肌很明显在工作

observations.observed: The user began distinguishing target-muscle effort from compensation and noticing which body region became fatigued first.
observations.response: Body-awareness itself became an explicit training target.

evidence: Clear target stretch was perceived in the kneeling-side upper thigh/groin.
A small pelvic repositioning cue changed where the stretch was felt.
tolerated: Supported half-kneeling position with knee padding
useful_cues: Tailbone subtly down / slight posterior pelvic tilt
Move the pelvis forward only a few centimeters
current_need: Build repeatable hip-flexor stretch positioning before adding rotational refinements
progression_gate: Target stretch remains clear without lumbar pinching or compensation

evidence: Anterior vs posterior tilt was understood through the pelvis-as-a-bowl cue.
useful_cues: Use a very small movement; do not force or permanently hold posterior tilt
current_need: Convert conceptual understanding into clearer embodied perception
progression_gate: Can deliberately move pelvis anterior/posterior without using the low back aggressively

evidence: Low back could stay stable during a small heel tap.
Core activation was difficult to perceive while shoulders/upper traps compensated.
provokes: Larger or more effortful versions increase shoulder/upper-trapezius participation
useful_cues: Hands on lower ribs/abdomen instead of pressing into the floor
Shoulders heavy and away from ears
Do not force the low back flat
current_need: Keep the movement small enough that trunk position remains stable
progression_gate: Heel tap remains stable with relaxed shoulders and neck
Core stabilization becomes easier to perceive

evidence: The user began identifying when a non-target region was the first to fatigue.
The user could distinguish stretch location and compensation more precisely than at the start of the session.
useful_cues: If exercise is meant to train A but B is first exhausted, suspect compensation before adding reps
current_need: Continue building a body map before increasing training intensity
progression_gate: Can reliably distinguish target effort, compensation, stretch, and discomfort across several basic movements

interpretation: The main state change was not workout volume but the beginning of a movement-control and proprioception rebuild.
Shoulders/upper traps currently tend to assist tasks that should be handled more by trunk control.
Conceptual understanding of pelvic positioning appeared ahead of fully automatic motor control.
safety_notes: Avoid aggressive jumping/HIIT during the initial rebuild phase.
Pain, sharp pinching, radiating symptoms, numbness/tingling, or weakness should not be treated as ordinary progression signals.
next_exposure: Repeat supported hip-flexor positioning at low intensity.
Use dead-bug regressions that keep shoulders relaxed before progressing range.
